subject: Moonlight Financial — sudden inference latency and errors / reserved throughput shortfall
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@moonlight-fin.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@moonlight-fin.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Aug 2029 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected latency + 5xx surge — we are throttled

Evelyn,

We started seeing a severe latency jump and a wave of 5xx errors hitting our production endpoints starting ~08:50 PDT. This is impacting the real-time scoring pipeline (median latency from 80ms to 1.6s, error rate ~7%). Our engineers pulled logs and saw repeated "quota exceeded"/"reservation throttle" messages in the responses. We are on a reserved capacity plan and our monitoring shows token consumption is within committed numbers, but the tenant is getting queued/aged in the GPU pool.

Attaching a small sample of stack traces and a CSV export of reserved usage. Can you confirm whether this is a pool saturation / noisy-neighbor situation or an internal throttling rule? We need a timeline for a mitigation path — this is customer-impacting and the ops team here is ready to jump on a call.

Samir
Head of Engineering
Moonlight Financial

Attachments: moonlight-5xx-sample.log, reserved-usage-20290812.csv

Samir — thank you for the quick heads up and the logs. I’m escalating to Ops and Engineering immediately. Quick summary of what I’m doing: 
- Looping in David (on-call infra lead) to run an immediate capacity check and queue inspection.
- Ben (account lead) will coordinate a short-term commercial remedy (burst credits or invoice hold) if we confirm reserved shortfall.
- Marissa (runtime eng) will look at KV cache eviction/ batching behavior for your tenant.

We’ll set up a 20-minute bridge in the next 15 minutes and send an interim update within 30. Our priority is restoring your production latency to baseline.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Samir Rao <samir@moonlight-fin.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Aug 2029 09:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency + 5xx surge — we are throttled

On the bridge now (logs attached). Immediate findings:
- Observed GPU pool saturation in zone us-west-2a between 08:40–09:10 PDT; queue depth increased by ~420% for inference workers hosting mixed tenants.
- Moonlight’s reservation shows committed tokens but their requests are routed to a pool that is simultaneously handling heavy burst traffic from unreserved workloads. We have a routing contention: policy allowed spillover into shared hotpath because the dedicated pool reached node-level CPU/KV pressure.
- There are frequent KV cache evictions for Moonlight (small model with large prefix reuse) causing repeated attention recomputation and higher per-request token work. That amplifies effective utilization.

Immediate mitigations we can push (short window):
1) Pin Moonlight to a quieter subset of nodes (requires rapid reprovisioning and may cause slight cold-start latencies) — ETA: 12–18 minutes.
2) Enforce per-tenant batching cap (disable large continuous aggregation for Moonlight) — ETA: 6 minutes (config change).
3) Failover to a slightly lower-capacity quantized model variant that runs with less memory pressure — ETA: 10–20 minutes.
4) As a last resort, temporarily throttle non-reserved burst traffic in the impacted pool (requires exec approval and will impact other customers).

Requesting:
- Ben/Revenue: immediate approval for a one-time burst credit if we need to move Moonlight to dedicated pinned nodes or provision transient capacity.
- Eng leadership: permission to perform the pin + model variant change now.

Attaching: dashboard_qps_spike.png for the queue and usage timeline sent by Samir.

—David
David Kim
Sr. Director, Platform Operations

Team / Samir — I’m on the line with finance; we can provision a short-term burst authorization (one-time) to immediately buy headroom while we remediate. Commercial proposal:
- One-time transient capacity credit to cover expected peak for the next 6 hours.
- If pinning to dedicated nodes is required, we can offer a discounted rate for the first 30 days as part of a temporary uplift amendment.

Need Evelyn or Exec to clear the transient capacity spend (est. cost $5–8k for the 6-hour window) OR authorization to throttle other burst customers in the pool for the next 2 hours while we pin and roll.

Samir — if you can confirm you want us to proceed with the transient credit, I’ll open the approval and notify accounting. If Moonlight prefers no commercial change, we will attempt the config pin + model variant failover and keep you posted.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Account Director, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 12 Aug 2029 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency + 5xx surge — we are throttled

Tech note / proposed action plan from runtime team: 
- Push config change to disable continuous batching for tenant moonlight-fin (reduces per-request KV pressure) — rolling config push, non-disruptive to other tenants. ETA: 6 minutes.
- Pin Moonlight workload to a 6-node dedicated subset with warmed caches; plan: live migration of routing table and a soft restart of worker processes. Risk: ~4–8% transient error increase during migration for in-flight requests. ETA: 18 minutes once we get transient credit or exec clearance for transient capacity.
- Failover model variant: we have a 4-bit quantized variant pre-validated against your evals; expected median latency reduction ~30% at similar quality for this workload. Requires model pinning and prompt-preservation check. ETA: 12 minutes.

I’ll coordinate the live steps and post play-by-play to the bridge. If Ben can confirm commercial approval we’ll execute pin + quantized model in parallel. If not, we’ll do batching cap + model variant first and then assess.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Manager, Runtime Engineering
